name: refetch_w1_worst
code:
def refetch_w1_worst(p, hw, cfg) -> float:
    """DRAM time / (2MNK/peak) of the operand-panel refetches of the worse width-1 raster (N-first refetches B panels, M-first A panels). A panel is shared only inside a lockstep window of one CTA per SM; a later window re-reads it unless the cyclic working set (whole fast-side panel K-slice + the co-resident slow panels + serial split-K partial round trips) fits in L2 (LRU step: fits -> hit, else miss). Larger is worse."""
    gm, gn, sk, b = math.ceil(p.M / cfg.tile_m), math.ceil(p.N / cfg.tile_n), max(1, cfg.split_k), p.bytes_per_element
    kp = math.ceil(p.K / (cfg.tile_k * sk)) * cfg.tile_k; L = hw.sm_count; W = L * max(1, cfg.max_blocks_per_sm)
    part = 2.0 * b * cfg.tile_m * cfg.tile_n * (sk - 1) / sk if cfg.split_k_mode == "serial" else 0.0
    t0 = 2.0 * p.M * p.N * p.K / (hw.peak_tflops_f16 * 1e12); bw = hw.bandwidth_gbps * 1e9
    return max((max(1.0, ns * min(1.0, nf / L)) - 1.0) * ext * p.K * b / bw / t0
               * float((ext + min(sl, math.ceil(W / nf) * ts)) * kp * b + max(W, nf) * part > hw.l2_bytes)
               for nf, ext, ns, ts, sl in ((gn, p.N, gm, cfg.tile_m, p.M), (gm, p.M, gn, cfg.tile_n, p.N)))
rationale: Worst-case width-1 raster panel refetch, in DRAM time over the ideal compute time 2MNK/peak (same unit as tm_dram_ratio, so a rule can add it to the DRAM leg). Without a raster field the rule cannot tell which width-1 order runs, so it prices the worse of the two: N-first (column-fastest) re-reads B panels once per slow row, M-first re-reads A panels. Sharing: consecutive CTAs that start together on different SMs run in K-lockstep, so a panel is fetched once per lockstep window of hw.sm_count CTAs (one CTA per SM; the other max_blocks_per_sm-1 co-resident CTAs of an SM are staggered, as in J2d's /resident_block_scarcity): fetches per fast-side panel per split slice = max(1, slow_tiles * min(1, fast_tiles / sm_count)). Between windows a panel survives only if the cyclic reuse fits L2. LRU on a cyclic stream larger than the cache misses on (almost) every access and a stream that fits hits, so the miss is a step (not 1 - L2/slice): working set = the whole fast-side operand K-slice (N or M rows * K-slice * b) + the slow panels of the co-resident set (ceil(sm_count*max_blocks_per_sm / fast_tiles) of them) + the serial split-K partial stream of the co-resident/cycle CTAs (each serial slice after the first reads and writes its partial tile: tile_m*tile_n*2b bytes, = 4 bytes/element for f16, averaged over sk slices). Refetch bytes = (fetches - 1) * fast-side operand bytes (unpadded: rows/columns beyond M or N are predicated off and move no DRAM bytes), so unlike a/b_refetch_bw_demand it does not shrink as split_k shrinks the K-slice: the partial stream keeps the working set above L2. All constants are hw.* or cfg.*/p.* quantities; 2 (read+write, FMA flops) and 1e9/1e12 are unit conversions.
